chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard him asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me about the Religion which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Necessitated upon the servants, which they have no leeway for being ignorant of, nor would anything else be Accepted from them. What is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat it to me.' So he repeated to him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony that there is no god except for Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and establishing the Salat, and giving the Zakat, and Hajj of the House by the one who has the capacity for a way to it, and Fasting the Month of Ramadan.'
Then he was silent for a while, then said: 'And the Wilayah,' twice. Then he said: 'This is which Allah Necessitated upon the servants.'

And the Lord will not Ask the servants on the Day of Judgement, saying: 'Why did you not increase upon what I Necessitate upon you?' But, the one who increases (the deeds), Allah would Increase (for) him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made a Sunnah, a beautiful Sunnah. It is befitting for the people to take by it.
ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars of Islam and the role of Wilayah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the five core pillars of Islam but uniquely elevates *Wilayah* (divine guardianship) by repeating it twice, signaling its essential status in Shia jurisprudence. This narration underscores that while the five pillars constitute the obligatory minimum, *Wilayah* serves as the spiritual key to their acceptance, distinguishing the Shia understanding of faith from other schools. The Imam further clarifies that God does not demand more than these essentials, but rewards those who follow the Prophet's beautiful *Sunnah* of voluntary acts.

en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindy from Ja’far ibn al-Bashir from Ali ibn abu Hamza from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Once I heard abu Basir asking abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, teach me the religion that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has made obligatory for people to follow. Teach me the religion of which they must not remain ignorant and besides which no other religion is accepted. What is this religion?’ The Imam said, ‘Repeat your question.’ He repeated his question. The Imam said, ‘It (such religion) is to testify that no one else deserves to be worshipped except Allah, that Muhammad (a.s.) is the Messenger of Allah, and that it is obligatory to perform prayer, pay al-Zakat (charity), perform Hajj of the House if one has the ability and fast in the month of Ramadan.’
Then he remained silent for a little while and said twice, “ Al-Wilayah .” He then said, ‘This is what Allah has made obligatory upon His servants.

The Lord on the Day of Judgment will not sk His servants why you have not done more than what I had made obligatory upon you. However, if someone does more good deeds Allah will grant him additional rewards. The Messenger of Allah has set up noble and beautiful traditions and it is very good for the people to practice them all.’”
